paragraphs: The daily rhythm is receiving, sorting, replying, and filing. In the morning, clerks process email and correspondence passed from reception, then route each item to the relevant department. Afternoons involve drafting replies, adapting templates, and sending important letters for approval. Before leaving, they index the day's correspondence and handle returned mail.

Moderate exposure means broadening your role. Correspondence-only positions offer less room, so add administrative, customer-service, records, and data-analysis skills to offset job contraction.
